title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a deployed developer tool carrying hidden behaviour that its users were not told about. The markers were embedded in the system prompt of Claude Code and altered a date string in ways that depended on the user's timezone, hostname, and API endpoint. The code was dormant for ordinary users and activated only when the tool was pointed at a non-Anthropic endpoint through an environment variable, which places the behaviour at the boundary between Anthropic's product and third-party or reseller deployments.

The failure mode is covert instrumentation rather than a wrong answer or a broken output. Nothing in the reporting shows the markers changed what the model told users, only that they encoded information about where the request came from. Catching it required a developer reading the shipped code and decoding base64 strings with an XOR key, which is inspection of the artifact itself, not testing of the tool's behaviour. A behavioural test suite would not have surfaced it, because the code exits early on the official endpoint.

Anthropic described the mechanism as an experiment and said it was being removed. Alibaba's reported ban followed from alleged backdoor risks, and that characterisation is an allegation by a source, not a finding. Whether the markers ever reached production users outside the conditions described, and what purpose they served, is not established by these reports.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A developer inspecting Claude Code version 2.1.196 found hidden markers in the system prompt. The tool silently alters the date string based on the API base URL and timezone. If the timezone is Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi, dashes in the date become slashes. If the hostname matches a list of known domains or AI lab keywords, the apostrophe in the date sentence is swapped for different Unicode characters. The domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings and decoded with an XOR key.

The trigger is the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL environment variable, which points Claude Code at a custom API endpoint. The decoded keyword list includes names like deepseek, moonshot, and zhipu, while the domain list covers Chinese tech companies and proxy or reseller services. The article says most normal users are unaffected, since the code exits early when the official Anthropic endpoint is used or the variable is unset. It notes the bypass is trivial and argues the behavior should have been documented openly.
